- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.33) in recent days, model tends to underestimate prices; increase forecast slightly.
- Model often overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days), especially if sentiment is neutral or positive — cap forecast at 10% above recent peak.
- Model underestimates mean-reverting periods — if 3-5 consecutive days show downward trend, add 2-3% upward bias to counteract mean reversion.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently misses late-period momentum — if sentiment turns positive after day 15, adjust forecast upward by 1-2% for days 16–30.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., +0.67, -0.33, +0.67), model tends to lag — add 1-2% buffer to forecast for next cycle.
